rules.text: prefix vowel, internal vowel, final ending and the form class of the source verb are SUPPLIED evidence; an unvocalized token supplies none of the vowel features and therefore resolves nothing
the prefix vowel is the only formal boundary between the tool class and the place-or-time class, so an unpointed prefix abstains and never defaults to the more frequent class
the derived-form verbal noun and the patient noun coincide in shape: where both are licensed, both are preserved and the function is decided by context outside this table
instrument templates are lexical, not derivable: this table classifies an attested token, it never predicts which template a root takes
a place-or-time reading presupposes a bare triliteral source; the same prefix vowel over a derived source is outside the table's regime
